rounds.text: Asset Reconstruction Company (India) Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.96x against a book value of ₹ 127 and a share price of ₹ 122 [E2]. Valuation metrics show it trading at a P/E of 10x [E1], which is notably lower than the sector benchmark P/E of 18.49x [E6], alongside an EV/EBITDA of 9.18x compared to the sector benchmark of 13.05x [E11]. Profitability and operating leverage are expanding sharply, highlighted by a quarterly operating margin of 82% in September 2026—a 16 percentage point increase over the year-ago quarter [E24]—and a screen flag pointing to net profit surging by 216% year-on-year [E53]. This strong operational turnaround is backed by robust cash generation, delivering ₹ 192 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E29]. A discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of ₹ 396 per share, providing a substantial margin of safety of 69.2% [E38, E39]. Conceded: borrowings have risen to ₹ 2,530 Cr in September 2026 from ₹ 1,206 Cr a year earlier [E32], and the current ratio sits at a low 0.49x as current liabilities exceed current assets [E31].

The bull case rests heavily on attractive headline valuation multiples and surging short-term profitability, but underlying financial health signals serious structural vulnerabilities [E1, E2, E6, E7, E53]. Most alarmingly, borrowings have more than doubled to Rs 2,530 Cr as of September 2026, up from Rs 1,206 Cr a year earlier, driving a severe liquidity imbalance where current liabilities exceed current assets with a current ratio of just 0.49x [E31, E32]. This aggressive debt accumulation accompanies a negative 3-year compounded sales growth rate of -4%, highlighting that medium-term top-line momentum has actually stalled despite recent quarterly spikes [E15]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is undermined by rising debtor days, which have lengthened from 41.6 to 53.6 days [E49]. Market sentiment actively reflects these concerns, keeping the stock depressed near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 11% to 14% of the way up, positioned below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E5, E41, E43]. Conceded: the company maintains a healthy dividend payout of 17.9% [E47] and trades at a low P/E of 10 alongside an operating margin expansion to 82% in September 2026 [E1, E24].

The bear points to surging borrowings of Rs 2,530 Cr and a low current ratio, but this capital deployment directly fuels a stellar operational engine generating Rs 194 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 192 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E28, E29, E31, E32]. While the bear highlights a three-year sales contraction, it ignores the powerful momentum of a 24% trailing twelve-month sales growth and a massive 153% YoY sales surge flagged by the screening engine [E15, E16, E51]. Conceded: debtor days have increased from 41.6 to 53.6 days [E49]. Furthermore, the bear's reliance on depressed moving averages and low 52-week range positioning dismisses a glaring fundamental disconnect where results score an exceptional 95 out of 100 on a 216% YoY net profit explosion [E5, E41, E43, E53, E55]. Finally, the market's heavy discounting of the stock—trading at a mere 0.96x book value and a 10x P/E against an 18.49x sector benchmark—creates an extreme margin of safety where today's price prices in a paltry 1.8% growth against an 18% base case [E1, E2, E6, E40].

Conceded: net profit grew 216% YoY and sales surged 153% YoY [E51, E53], but these eye-catching figures mask a deeper multi-year decay where 3-year compounded sales growth sits deeply negative at -4% [E15]. The bull champions operational cash flows of Rs 194 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 192 Cr [E28, E29], yet completely ignores that borrowings more than doubled to a staggering Rs 2,530 Cr by September 2026 alongside a precarious current ratio of 0.49x where current liabilities severely exceed current assets [E31, E32]. Furthermore, dismissing the stock's slump near its 52-week lows and below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages as "stale sentiment" [E5, E41, E43, E55] ignores persistent fundamental vulnerabilities, including ballooning debtor days from 41.6 to 53.6 days [E49] and a low 3-year return on equity of just 10.3% [E48]. Finally, the claim of an extreme margin of safety and a consistent dividend payout [E40, E47] is entirely undermined by a zero percent dividend yield [E4] and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E25] that signals underlying operational volatility rather than durable compounding.
